clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-686 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8555-exemption-samuel-cottrell-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed September 28, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of nine months, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of nine months ending June 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8262 of September 26, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, June 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of nine months ending June 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of June 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when June 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8805, signed June 25, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("Executive Orders No. 8262 of September 26, 1939, and No. 8555 of September 28, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending June 30, 1942". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. MOMMSEN-I rechecked this stated end against both held witnesses.
